snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ SSC Biology Hook: Mito: Power. Small Intestine: Absorption. O-: Donor. Nephron: Kidney. Neuron: Nerve. Xylem: Water. 120/80: Normal BP. ⚡ v12 Stamina Hook: 60-min Sprint active.

quick_notes.title: Cell Recap
quick_notes.detail: Mito (Power), Lyso (Suicide), Ribo (Protein). Robert Hooke (Cell). Plant (Wall), whereas Animal (No wall).
quick_notes.explanation: A cell is the basic building block of all living things. Robert Hooke was the scientist who first discovered and named cells in the 1660s. Inside a cell, there are tiny parts called organelles that each have a specific job. The mitochondria, often called the powerhouse of the cell, produce energy for the cell to use. Lysosomes act as the cell's cleanup crew, breaking down waste and old parts, which is why they are sometimes called the suicide bags of the cell. Ribosomes are the protein factories that build proteins, which the cell needs to grow and repair itself. A key difference between plant and animal cells is that plant cells have a rigid cell wall outside their membrane for support, while animal cells do not have a cell wall.

quick_notes.title: Digestion Recap
quick_notes.detail: Mouth (Amylase), Stomach (Pepsin), Small Intestine (Absorption). Liver (Largest gland). Bile stored in Gall bladder.
quick_notes.explanation: Digestion begins in the mouth, where an enzyme called amylase breaks down starches into sugars. In the stomach, a different enzyme called pepsin digests proteins. The small intestine is where most nutrients are absorbed into the bloodstream. The liver is the largest gland in the body, and it produces a liquid called bile that helps digest fats. The gallbladder is a small organ that stores the bile until it is needed in the small intestine.

quick_notes.title: Circulation Recap
quick_notes.detail: Heart (4 chambers). RBC (120 days/Hemoglobin). O- (Donor), AB+ (Recipient). Sphygmomanometer (BP).
quick_notes.explanation: The human heart has four chambers: two upper atria and two lower ventricles, which pump blood through the body. Red blood cells (RBCs) live for about 120 days and contain hemoglobin, a protein that carries oxygen from the lungs to all tissues. For blood transfusions, O negative (O-) blood type has no A, B, or Rh proteins on its surface, so it can be donated to any person, making it the universal donor. AB positive (AB+) blood type has all these proteins, so a person with AB+ can receive blood from any donor, making them the universal recipient. A sphygmomanometer is a device with an inflatable cuff and a pressure gauge used to measure blood pressure, which is the force of blood against artery walls.

quick_notes.title: Excretion Recap
quick_notes.detail: Kidney (Nephron). Urea produced in Liver, filtered by Kidney. Dialysis (Artificial filtration).
quick_notes.explanation: Excretion is the process of removing waste from the body. Urea is a waste chemical formed in the liver from the breakdown of proteins. The kidneys filter this urea out of the blood using tiny units called nephrons, which are the basic filtering parts inside each kidney. Dialysis is an artificial filtration treatment that cleans the blood when a person's kidneys are not working properly.

quick_notes.title: Plant Tissue Recap
quick_notes.explanation: Plant tissues are groups of cells that work together to perform specific jobs. Xylem is a type of tissue that carries water from the roots to the rest of the plant. Phloem is another tissue that transports food made in the leaves to all other parts of the plant. Meristematic tissue is found in areas where the plant is growing, like the tips of roots and shoots, and it allows the plant to increase in length and produce new cells.

lesson_intro: Today we consolidate the 'Foundations of Life'. You have mastered the cell nicknames, the digestive path, the heart's rhythm, and the kidney's filtration. In SSC Science, Biology accounts for the maximum questions. Today, we drill the facts. If you see 'Powerhouse', you say 'Mito'. If you see 'Universal Donor', you say 'O-'. Let's lock in the biology marks today.
